_comment: Warframe slang, abbreviations and shorthand a player meets in the UI, tooltips, trade chat and build videos. term -> plain-language meaning, written for someone who has never played. Used by warframe_glossary. Keep it to one or two sentences - the point is to unblock, not to lecture.

entries.MR: Mastery Rank - your account-wide level, raised by levelling NEW gear to 30 for the first time. It gates which weapons, quests, Riven mods and syndicates you can access. Levelling the same item again (e.g. after Forma) gives no MR.
entries.mastery rank: Your account-wide level, raised by levelling new gear to 30 the first time. Gates weapons, quests, Rivens and trade limits. Re-levelling an already-mastered item gives nothing.
entries.affinity: Experience points. Kill enemies, complete objectives and use abilities to earn it; it levels up whatever gear is equipped. Squadmates share affinity within 50m (shared affinity radius).
entries.endo: The resource used to upgrade mods. Comes from dissolving duplicate mods, from Ayatan Sculptures, and from high-level mission rewards. Early on this is your main bottleneck.
entries.credits: The common soft currency - crafting, blueprints from the Market, and trading fees. Never spend Platinum on anything you can buy with Credits.
entries.plat: Platinum - the premium currency. Also the player-to-player trading currency, which means you can earn it for free by trading. Do NOT spend it on items from the in-game Market.
entries.platinum: The premium currency, and the currency players trade in. Earnable for free by trading with other players. Spend it on Warframe and weapon SLOTS first, and on cosmetics if you like them.
entries.forma: Resets an item to rank 0 and lets you add or change a polarity on one mod slot, permanently halving the drain of matching mods. The core of endgame build crafting - expect to use several per item.
entries.polarity: The symbol on a mod slot. A mod whose polarity matches the slot costs half as much capacity. Mismatched mods cost more. This is why Forma exists.
entries.potato: Community slang for an Orokin Catalyst (weapon) or Orokin Reactor (Warframe) - an item that DOUBLES an item's mod capacity. Called a potato because it's starchy and boring but you need it.
entries.orokin catalyst: Doubles a WEAPON's mod capacity. Blueprint comes from Nightwave, Invasions, alerts and events. Slang: potato.
entries.orokin reactor: Doubles a WARFRAME's mod capacity. Blueprint comes from Nightwave, Invasions, alerts and events. Slang: potato.
entries.riven: A Riven Mod - a randomly generated, randomly rolled weapon mod with a challenge to unlock it ('veiled' -> 'unveiled'). Only drops from Sorties, Eidolon hunts and similar. The main way players make Platinum.
entries.riven mod: A randomly generated weapon mod, unique per weapon family, that must be unlocked by completing a challenge. Can be re-rolled with Kuva. Highly variable - most are junk, good ones are worth a lot.
entries.kuva: A resource used to re-roll Riven mods, and to build Kuva weapons from the Kuva Fortress. Farmed from Kuva missions, Kuva Survival and Kuva Floods.
entries.kuva lich: A personal nemesis you create by executing a Kuva Larvling. It steals your mission rewards until you hunt it down by collecting Requiem mods and stabbing it in the right order.
entries.sister of parvos: The Corpus version of a Kuva Lich - created in the Granum Void, steals your rewards, hunted the same way.
entries.incarnon: A weapon upgrade path unlocked in The Circuit (Duviri). Installing an Incarnon Genesis adapter on an older weapon gives it a transformative alternate form and big stat boosts. Often best-in-class.
entries.incarnon genesis: The adapter that grants a weapon its Incarnon form and evolutions. Bought from the Duviri/Circuit vendor with Pathos Clamps.
entries.archon shard: A shard installed into a Warframe via the Helminth that grants a permanent bonus (ability strength, duration, health, armour, energy, casting speed). From Archon Hunts, Netracells and Deep Archimedea.
entries.tauforged: A stronger version of an Archon Shard, made by merging five identical shards. Roughly 1.5x the effect.
entries.helminth: The infested room in your Orbiter. Its main use is SUBSUME: sacrifice a Warframe to unlock one of its abilities, then inject that ability onto a different Warframe.
entries.subsume: Feed a (non-Prime) Warframe to the Helminth to permanently unlock one of its signature abilities for use on other Warframes. The sacrificed frame is destroyed. This is irreversible - check before you do it.
entries.steel path: A harder version of the entire Star Chart, unlocked after completing the normal one. Enemies start much higher level and have more armour, and it drops Steel Essence and special arcanes.
entries.sp: Steel Path - the harder replay of the whole Star Chart, unlocked after you clear the normal chart.
entries.steel essence: The Steel Path currency, spent at Teshin for arcanes, relics, cosmetics and Kuva.
entries.arbitration: A rotating high-level endless mission with no shields for the Warframe and automatic revives. Drops Vitus Essence and the Acolyte arcanes.
entries.arbi: Arbitration - high-level rotating endless mission that drops Vitus Essence.
entries.eso: Elite Sanctuary Onslaught - a fast wave-clear mode that is the standard way to farm Focus and to power-level weapons.
entries.so: Sanctuary Onslaught - the normal version of ESO, used for levelling.
entries.tridolon: The three Eidolons on the Plains of Eidolon, fought in sequence at night: Teralyst, Gantulyst, Hydrolyst. The classic late-game Arcanes and Focus farm.
entries.eidolon: The giant Sentient constructs on the Plains of Eidolon, fought at night. Your normal weapons barely scratch them - you need the Operator's Amp.
entries.focus: A post-The-War-Within progression system. You install a Lens on gear to convert excess affinity into Focus points, then spend them in one of five Focus Schools.
entries.focus school: One of five passive skill trees: Zenurik (energy), Naramon (melee crit / affinity), Madurai (ability and amp damage), Vazarin (healing and revive), Unairu (armour strip and survivability). Zenurik is the usual first pick.
entries.zenurik: The energy Focus School - its Energizing Dash is the standard answer to 'I'm always out of energy'. Usually the first school players max.
entries.lens: An item installed on a max-rank weapon or Warframe that converts excess affinity into Focus. Different Lens tiers convert at different rates.
entries.operator: Your Tenno's void-self - the child you control outside of a Warframe after The War Within. Used for Eidolons, some puzzles, and energy regeneration.
entries.drifter: Your adult Tenno self, met in Duviri. Separate from the Operator but uses the same Amp and focus.
entries.amp: The Operator's weapon. Built from parts from the Quills (Cetus) or Vox Solaris (Fortuna). Essential for Eidolon hunts - Warframe weapons do almost nothing to Eidolon shields.
entries.railjack: Your clan's spaceship, used for space missions. Levelled with Intrinsics (crew ranks) and Avionics (ship mods). Needed for several quests and for the fastest credits in the game.
entries.intrinsics: Railjack crew ranks: Tactical, Piloting, Gunnery, Engineering, Command. Levelled with Intrinsic Points from Railjack missions.
entries.necramech: A piloted mechanical exosuit, mostly used on Deimos (Isolation Vaults) and in some Railjack content. Voidrig and Bonewidow are the two frames.
entries.duviri: The open-world roguelite zone. You play as the Drifter with randomised gear and pick up Decrees (stacking buffs) as you go.
entries.circuit: The Circuit - a roguelite mode inside Duviri with randomised Warframes and weapons. Completing it earns the currency for Incarnon Genesis adapters. Steel Path Circuit gives better rewards.
entries.decree: A stacking buff you choose between runs in Duviri and The Circuit. They are what make underpowered random loadouts viable.
entries.relic: A Void Relic - contains Prime parts. Refine it with Void Traces to raise rare-chances, then open it in a Void Fissure mission. The main way to get Prime gear.
entries.void relic: Contains Prime parts. Refine it with Void Traces to improve the odds of the rare part, then crack it in a Void Fissure.
entries.fissure: A Void Fissure - a mission where you open a Relic by collecting Reactant from corrupted enemies. Everyone picks from all relics opened, so a squad is far more efficient than solo.
entries.radshare: A squad where all four players bring the same RADIANT-refined relic, maximising the chance someone gets the rare part. The standard way to hunt a specific Prime part.
entries.vaulted: A Prime whose relics no longer drop from normal missions. Vaulted Primes return periodically through Prime Resurgence.
entries.prime resurgence: A rotating event where vaulted Primes return, bought with Aya (free, farmed) or Regal Aya (paid).
entries.aya: A currency from Void missions used during Prime Resurgence to buy vaulted relics and cosmetics. Regal Aya is the paid version.
entries.ducats: What you get for selling Prime parts to a relay's Ducat Kiosk. Spent at Baro Ki'Teer. The main sink for worthless duplicate Prime parts.
entries.baro: Baro Ki'Teer, the Void Trader - appears at a random relay every two weeks and sells exclusive Primed mods, weapons and cosmetics for Ducats + Credits.
entries.syndicate: A faction you earn Standing with by wearing their sigil or doing their missions. Standing buys faction-specific mods, weapons and arcanes. Each has a daily cap based on your MR.
entries.standing: Faction reputation. Earned daily up to a cap that scales with Mastery Rank, then spent on that faction's rewards.
entries.nightwave: The free battle pass. Completing weekly and daily acts earns creds spent on Nitain Extract, Orokin Catalyst/Reactor blueprints, helmets, cosmetics and weapon slots.
entries.arcane: An enhancement socketed into a Warframe, Operator, or amp. Grants effects like health on headshot, damage resistance, or energy on kill. Many of the strongest ones come from Eidolons, Steel Path and Netracells.
entries.mod: Upgradable cards that define every build: damage, survivability, ability stats. Mod capacity is THE limiting resource on every item.
entries.galvanized mods: A powerful mod family bought with Vitus Essence (Arbitrations). They gain large stacking bonuses on kill and are the backbone of most endgame weapon builds.
entries.archon mods: Mods from Archon Hunts that add a scaling effect keyed to an ability, e.g. Archon Vitality boosting heat-status damage.
entries.umbral mods: A three-piece set (Umbral Vitality / Fiber / Intensify) that becomes far stronger when several are equipped together, but costs extra capacity unless the slot is Umbra-polarised.
entries.primed mods: Stronger versions of core mods. Mostly sold by Baro Ki'Teer for Ducats, or given as a daily login reward over time.
entries.corrupted mods: Mods with a large bonus and a matching penalty (e.g. +duration, -efficiency), found in the Orokin Derelict Dragon Vaults on Deimos. Essential for min-maxing.
entries.nightmare mods: Dual-stat mods from Nightmare missions (harder missions with a random penalty). Common early power spikes.
entries.aura: A Warframe mod that ADDs capacity instead of draining it. A properly polarised Aura is free mod capacity.
entries.exilus: An extra Warframe mod slot for utility mods (sprint speed, bullet jump, enemy radar). Usually unlocked with an Exilus Adapter.
entries.status chance: The odds a hit applies a status effect. Status damage types (Viral, Slash, Heat, Corrosive) are the backbone of late-game weapon builds.
entries.viral: A combined element (Cold + Toxin) that multiplies damage to health and stacks up to 10 times. The single most-used damage type for general play.
entries.slash: An elemental-less damage type whose proc applies a bleeding DoT that ignores armour. Strong against heavily armoured enemies.
entries.heat: A elemental damage type whose proc deals damage over time and partially strips armour. Very strong and heavily used.
entries.corrosive: A combined element (Toxin + Electricity) that strips armour. Strong against Grineer.
entries.armor strip: Removing enemy armour so your damage actually lands. Done with abilities, Corrosive/Heat procs or Unairu. The main reason early weapons stop working around level 50+.
entries.shield gating: When your shields break you get a brief window of invulnerability. Advanced survivability technique used at very high levels where armour and health stop mattering.
entries.co: Condition Overload - a melee mod that scales damage per unique status type on the target. The reason 'COBWEB' builds stack many statuses.
entries.cobweb: A melee build acronym: Condition Overload, Blood Rush, Weeping Wounds, and Organ Shatter/Berserker. The classic crit-status melee setup.
entries.nuke frame: A Warframe built to clear whole rooms with abilities (Saryn, Volt, Equinox, Mesa, Gauss). Fast for farming but often fragile.
entries.tenno: You - the player character, and the faction you belong to.
entries.orokin: The ancient lost civilisation whose ruins, towers and relics are everywhere. Source of most Prime gear and Orokin Cells.
entries.grineer: The cloned soldier faction. Heavily armoured - use Corrosive, Heat or armour strip.
entries.corpus: The corporate faction with shields and robotics. Use Toxin to bypass shields.
entries.infested: The swarm faction. Weak to Heat and Slash, and they swarm in melee.
entries.sentient: The Orokin's ancient self-adapting enemies. They adapt to repeated damage types, which is why you swap weapons against them.
entries.archon: The boss-tier enemies introduced with Veilbreaker, fought in Archon Hunts. Drop Archon Shards and Archon mods.
entries.open world: The large free-roam zones: Plains of Eidolon (Cetus), Orb Vallis (Fortuna), Cambion Drift (Deimos), Zariman, Sanctum Anatomica and Duviri. Each has its own vendors, bounties and grind.
entries.bounty: A repeatable contract in an open-world zone. The main way to earn that zone's standing and resource rewards.
entries.simulacrum: A test room unlocked from Cephalon Simaris where you spawn enemies to test builds without risking a mission.
entries.conclave: The PvP mode. Largely inactive - do not judge the game by it.
entries.mr fodder: Weapons built and levelled to 30 purely for Mastery Rank, then sold or discarded.
entries.leech: A player who contributes nothing and lets the squad carry them. Mildly rude; do not assume a struggling new player is one.
entries.carry: Letting a much stronger player do the work in a mission so you can clear or level quickly.
entries.tenet: Corpus-origin adversary weapons, from Sisters of Parvos, that come with a bonus elemental damage type.
entries.coda: Technocyte Coda - the Infested-era adversary weapons, with their own hunt loop.
entries.netracell: A weekly high-level mission that drops Archon Shards, and one of the most efficient weekly activities once you are geared.
entries.deep archimedea: A weekly high-level mission chain with modifiers, rewarding Archon Shards and Vosfor.
entries.vosfor: A currency earned from weekly activities, spent on Arcane packs at the Sanctum Anatomica vendor.
